source.text: τῇ ἐλευθερίᾳ ἡμᾶς Χριστὸς ἠλευθέρωσεν· στήκετε οὖν καὶ μὴ πάλιν ζυγῷ δουλείας ἐνέχεσθε.

records.literal_gloss: For the freedom us Christ set free; stand firm therefore and not again in a yoke of slavery be held.

en.L: For freedom {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} set us free; stand firm therefore, and do not again be held fast in a yoke of slavery.
en.B: Freedom was {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}'s purpose when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} set us free. So stand firm, and do not let yourselves be held again under a yoke of slavery.
en.R: {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} set us free so that we would live as free people. So stand firm. Do not let anyone put a slave's yoke on you again.

es.L: Para [la] libertad {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} nos hizo libres; {{plural_you:manténganse|manteneos}} firmes, pues, y no {{plural_you:estén|estéis}} otra vez sujetos a un yugo de esclavitud.
es.B: Para vivir en libertad nos liberó {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}. Así que {{plural_you:manténganse|manteneos}} firmes, y no {{plural_you:se dejen|os dejéis}} atar de nuevo bajo un yugo de esclavitud.
es.R: {{christos:Cristo|El Mesías}} nos liberó para que vivamos como personas libres. Por eso, {{plural_you:manténganse|manteneos}} firmes. No {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que nadie {{plural_you:les|os}} vuelva a poner un yugo de esclavos.

sw.L: Kwa ajili ya uhuru {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alituweka huru; kwa hiyo simameni imara, wala msifungwe tena katika nira ya utumwa.
sw.B: {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alituweka huru ili tuishi katika uhuru. Kwa hiyo simameni imara, wala msikubali kufungwa tena chini ya nira ya utumwa.
sw.R: {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alituweka huru ili tuishi kama watu huru. Kwa hiyo simameni imara. Msikubali mtu yeyote awawekee tena nira ya utumwa.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "for freedom Christ set us free" as a sentence of its own
alternatives: "stand firm in the freedom with which Christ set us free", joining the clause to the command
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add a relative word and make the opening part of the command to stand firm, the reading behind the King James Version. The SBLGNT text, with the earliest manuscripts, has a complete statement followed by a raised dot, then the command. Either way Paul says that Christ has freed them and they must hold on to that freedom.

decisions.choice: "for freedom": freedom is the purpose of Christ's act
alternatives: "with freedom" or "by freedom": freedom as the means
decisions.reason: The dative τῇ ἐλευθερίᾳ stands first for emphasis beside the verb from the same root (ἐλευθερόω). Paul is saying what Christ freed them for: to live as free people, not to pass from one slavery into another. The word picks up the free woman and her children of 4:22-31.

decisions.choice: a yoke of slavery: the law taken up as a burden that binds
decisions.reason: A yoke is the wooden bar laid on the necks of working animals, and it was a common picture for being under another's rule. ἐνέχεσθε means to be held fast or caught in something. "Again" tells Gentile believers that taking the law as their master would be like returning to the slavery they knew under the elemental powers (4:3, 4:8-9).

decisions.choice: freedom stated first as the purpose
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say outright that freedom was the purpose, since the bare phrase is unclear in plain English.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: Paul writes to the Galatian churches in the plural throughout. Each plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain), as in Romans.

decisions.choice: slavery (L, B); a slave's yoke (R)
decisions.reason: "Slavery" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slavery under the law is set against freedom (m3).

source.text: Ἴδε ἐγὼ Παῦλος λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐὰν περιτέμνησθε Χριστὸς ὑμᾶς οὐδὲν ὠφελήσει.

records.literal_gloss: Look, I Paul say to you that if you are circumcised, Christ you nothing will profit.

en.L: Look, I, Paul, say to you that if you get circumcised, {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} will profit you nothing.
en.B: Listen! I, Paul, am telling you: if you have yourselves circumcised, {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} will do you no good at all.
en.R: Listen to me! I, Paul, am telling you this: if you go ahead and get circumcised, {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} will be of no use to you at all.

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}: yo, Pablo, {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que si {{plural_you:se circuncidan|os circuncidáis}}, {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} no {{plural_you:les|os}} servirá de nada.
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}! Yo, Pablo, {{plural_you:les|os}} aseguro: si {{plural_you:se hacen|os hacéis}} circuncidar, {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} no {{plural_you:les|os}} servirá absolutamente de nada.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Escúchenme|Escuchadme}}! Yo, Pablo, {{plural_you:les|os}} digo esto: si {{plural_you:siguen|seguís}} adelante y {{plural_you:se circuncidan|os circuncidáis}}, {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} no {{plural_you:les|os}} servirá para nada.

sw.L: Tazama, mimi Paulo nawaambia kwamba ikiwa mtatahiriwa, {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} hatawafaa chochote.
sw.B: Sikilizeni! Mimi Paulo nawaambia: mkikubali kutahiriwa, {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} hatakuwa na faida yoyote kwenu.
sw.R: Nisikilizeni! Mimi Paulo nawaambia hivi: mkiendelea na kukubali kutahiriwa, {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} hatawasaidia hata kidogo.

decisions.choice: circumcision taken up as a requirement for belonging to God's people
alternatives: circumcision as a mere physical rite with no further meaning
decisions.reason: The present tense of περιτέμνησθε speaks of Gentile believers who would now undergo circumcision because the agitators said they must (6:12-13). Paul himself had Timothy circumcised (Acts 16:3), so the rite as such is not the issue (5:6); taking it on as a condition of standing before God is, as verses 3-4 explain.

decisions.choice: Paul stakes his own authority on the warning
decisions.reason: Ἴδε calls for attention, and Paul names himself with the emphatic "I". He writes as the apostle who first brought them the gospel (1:1, 4:13).

decisions.choice: if you go ahead and get circumcised
decisions.reason: Readable brings out the present tense: a step the Galatians were thinking of taking.

source.text: μαρτύρομαι δὲ πάλιν παντὶ ἀνθρώπῳ περιτεμνομένῳ ὅτι ὀφειλέτης ἐστὶν ὅλον τὸν νόμον ποιῆσαι.

records.literal_gloss: And I testify again to every man being circumcised that a debtor he is the whole the law to do.

en.L: And I testify again to every man who gets circumcised that he is a debtor to do the whole law.
en.B: I insist once more to every man who has himself circumcised: he puts himself under obligation to carry out the entire law.
en.R: I will say it again to every man who gets circumcised: he then has to obey every part of the law.

es.L: Y de nuevo declaro solemnemente a todo hombre que se circuncida que es deudor de cumplir toda la ley.
es.B: Insisto una vez más ante todo hombre que se hace circuncidar: queda obligado a cumplir la ley entera.
es.R: Lo repito a todo hombre que se circuncida: desde ese momento tiene que obedecer cada parte de la ley.

sw.L: Tena nashuhudia kwa kila mtu anayetahiriwa kwamba yeye ni mdaiwa wa kuitenda sheria yote.
sw.B: Nasisitiza tena kwa kila mwanamume anayekubali kutahiriwa: amejifunga kuitimiza sheria nzima.
sw.R: Narudia tena kwa kila mwanamume anayetahiriwa: basi analazimika kutii kila sehemu ya sheria.

decisions.choice: under obligation, bound like a debtor to pay in full
alternatives: a debtor in a merely financial sense
decisions.reason: ὀφειλέτης is someone who owes a debt. Circumcision was the sign of the covenant given through Moses, so a man who takes it on as a requirement takes on the whole law with it. Paul has already said that the law curses everyone who does not keep all of it (3:10).

decisions.choice: "again" repeats the warning of verse 2
alternatives: "again" recalls an earlier warning given in person
decisions.reason: Paul restates verse 2 with a solemn word of testimony; he may also be recalling what he told them when he was with them. The point is the same.

decisions.choice: has himself circumcised / gets circumcised
decisions.reason: The Greek is a present participle in the middle or passive voice: a man who has the rite done to him.

source.text: κατηργήθητε ἀπὸ Χριστοῦ οἵτινες ἐν νόμῳ δικαιοῦσθε, τῆς χάριτος ἐξεπέσατε.

records.literal_gloss: You were severed from Christ, you who in law are being justified; from the grace you fell away.

en.L: You were cut off from {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, you who are being justified in [the] law; you have fallen away from grace.
en.B: Any of you who look to the law to justify you have been cut off from {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}; you have fallen away from grace.
en.R: If you are trying to be put right with God by keeping the law, you have cut yourselves off from {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. You have left God's grace behind.

es.L: {{plural_you:Han|Habéis}} sido separados {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} los que {{plural_you:son|sois}} justificados en [la] ley; de la gracia {{plural_you:han|habéis}} caído.
es.B: Los que {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}} ser justificados por la ley {{plural_you:han|habéis}} quedado desligados {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}; {{plural_you:han|habéis}} caído de la gracia.
es.R: Si {{plural_you:tratan|tratáis}} de ser declarados justos ante Dios cumpliendo la ley, {{plural_you:se han apartado|os habéis apartado}} {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}. {{plural_you:Han|Habéis}} dejado atrás la gracia de Dios.

sw.L: Mmekatiliwa mbali na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, ninyi mnaohesabiwa haki katika sheria; mmeanguka nje ya neema.
sw.B: Ninyi mnaotafuta kuhesabiwa haki kwa sheria mmekatiliwa mbali na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}; mmeanguka nje ya neema.
sw.R: Mkijaribu kuhesabiwa haki mbele za Mungu kwa kushika sheria, mmejitenga na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Mmeiacha nyuma neema ya Mungu.

decisions.choice: justify: God declares a person to be in the right before him, acquitted and accepted
alternatives: to make a person morally good
decisions.reason: δικαιόω is a courtroom word. Galatians uses it for God's verdict that a person stands right with him (2:16-17, 3:8, 3:11, 3:24). Here Paul speaks of looking for that verdict "in law", by keeping it.

decisions.choice: "you who are trying to be justified": the present tense describes an attempt
alternatives: "you who are justified by the law", as a fact
decisions.reason: Paul has said that no one is justified by the law (2:16, 3:11), so the present δικαιοῦσθε describes what they are trying to do, not something achieved. οἵτινες ("you who", "whoever of you") points to any of them who take that path.

decisions.choice: cut off from Christ, with the bond to him made void
alternatives: "you have no more use for Christ"
decisions.reason: καταργέω with "from" means to be released or severed from something, so that it no longer has effect. Romans 7:2 and 7:6 use it of being released from the law. To seek justification by the law is to break the tie with Christ that faith made.

decisions.choice: fallen away from grace: lost hold of the gift by which God accepts them
alternatives: "fallen from grace" as moral failure or loss of reputation
decisions.reason: ἐκπίπτω means to fall out of or lose one's place. Grace here is God's free gift of acceptance (1:6, 2:21); someone who relies on the law has stepped out of the place where grace is received. Paul is not speaking of an ordinary sin.

decisions.choice: put right with God
decisions.reason: Readable says what the courtroom word means in plain words; Literal and Balanced keep "justified".

decisions.choice: kuhesabiwa haki at every level
decisions.reason: As in Romans, Swahili keeps "kuhesabiwa haki" (to be counted righteous) for this verb at every level, so the reader can follow Paul's argument across Galatians and Romans. The phrase is already plain Swahili for God's verdict; Readable only adds "mbele za Mungu" where the English Readable says "put right with God".

source.text: ἡμεῖς γὰρ πνεύματι ἐκ πίστεως ἐλπίδα δικαιοσύνης ἀπεκδεχόμεθα.

records.literal_gloss: We for by [the] Spirit from faith [the] hope of righteousness eagerly await.

en.L: For we, by [the] Spirit, from faith, eagerly await [the] hope of righteousness.
en.B: But we, by the Spirit and on the ground of faith, are eagerly waiting for the righteousness we hope for.
en.R: But we, by the Spirit and through faith, wait eagerly for what we hope for: to hear God declare us righteous.

es.L: Porque nosotros, por [el] Espíritu, por [la] fe, aguardamos con anhelo [la] esperanza de [la] justicia.
es.B: Pero nosotros, por el Espíritu y sobre la base de la fe, esperamos con anhelo la justicia que es nuestra esperanza.
es.R: Pero nosotros, por el Espíritu y por medio de la fe, esperamos con ansias lo que anhelamos: oír a Dios declararnos justos.

sw.L: Kwa maana sisi, kwa Roho, kutokana na imani, tunalingoja kwa hamu tumaini la haki.
sw.B: Lakini sisi, kwa Roho na kwa msingi wa imani, tunaingoja kwa hamu haki tunayoitumainia.
sw.R: Lakini sisi, kwa msaada wa Roho na kupitia imani, tunangoja kwa hamu kile tunachotumainia: kumsikia Mungu akitutangaza kuwa wenye haki.

decisions.choice: by the Spirit: God's Spirit, given when they believed
decisions.reason: πνεύματι without the article still means God's Spirit, as in 3:3, 3:5 and 4:6: the Galatians received the Spirit by believing, not by doing what the law commands.

decisions.choice: the hope of righteousness: the righteousness hoped for, God's final verdict at the last day
alternatives: the hope that comes from being righteous now
decisions.reason: ἐλπίδα δικαιοσύνης most likely names what is hoped for: God's verdict of righteous, already given to faith (2:16) and still to be pronounced at the end. Paul could also mean the hope that belongs to those already made righteous. The two readings overlap: the Spirit and faith, not the law, carry believers to that day.

decisions.choice: "we" is emphatic, setting believers against those relying on the law
decisions.reason: ἡμεῖς stands first and is not needed for the verb. Paul sets "we" who wait by faith against "you who are trying to be justified in law" (verse 4).

decisions.choice: to hear God declare us righteous
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the reading chosen in m2; Literal and Balanced keep the phrase.

source.text: ἐν γὰρ Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ οὔτε περιτομή τι ἰσχύει οὔτε ἀκροβυστία, ἀλλὰ πίστις δι’ ἀγάπης ἐνεργουμένη.

records.literal_gloss: In for Christ Jesus neither circumcision anything is strong nor uncircumcision, but faith through love working.

en.L: For in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus neither circumcision has any force nor uncircumcision, but faith working through love.
en.B: For in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, being circumcised or uncircumcised counts for nothing. What counts is faith at work through love.
en.R: When we belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, it does not matter at all whether we are circumcised or not. What matters is faith that shows itself in love.

es.L: Porque en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}} ni la circuncisión tiene fuerza alguna ni la incircuncisión, sino [la] fe que obra por medio del amor.
es.B: Porque en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}} no cuenta para nada estar circuncidado o no estarlo. Lo que cuenta es la fe que se pone en acción por medio del amor.
es.R: Cuando pertenecemos {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}}, no importa en absoluto si estamos circuncidados o no. Lo que importa es la fe que se demuestra amando.

sw.L: Kwa maana katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu tohara haina nguvu yoyote, wala kutotahiriwa, bali imani inayotenda kazi kupitia upendo.
sw.B: Kwa maana katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, tohara au kutotahiriwa havina thamani yoyote. Kinachohesabika ni imani inayofanya kazi kwa njia ya upendo.
sw.R: Tukiwa wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, haijalishi hata kidogo kama tumetahiriwa au hatujatahiriwa. Kinachojalisha ni imani inayojionyesha katika upendo.

decisions.choice: faith working through love: faith shows its power in love
decisions.reason: ἐνεργουμένη is middle in sense here, as ἐνεργέω usually is in Paul: faith is active, and love is the way it works. The other reading, that love brings faith to life, puts the stress where Paul does not; faith is what justifies (2:16) and love is what it produces (5:13-14).

decisions.choice: circumcision and uncircumcision: being a Jew or a Gentile
decisions.reason: ἀκροβυστία literally means "foreskin", and Paul uses the pair for the two groups (2:7). In Christ neither condition gives a person any standing; 6:15 says the same.

decisions.choice: what counts is
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the verb from the first clause ("has any power") so that the contrast reads clearly.

source.text: Ἐτρέχετε καλῶς· τίς ὑμᾶς ἐνέκοψεν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ μὴ πείθεσθαι;

records.literal_gloss: You were running well; who you cut in on to the truth not to obey?

en.L: You were running well; who cut in on you so that you do not obey the truth?
en.B: You had been running a good race. Who got in your way and turned you from obeying the truth?
en.R: You were doing so well, like runners in a race. Who blocked your way and stopped you from following the truth?

es.L: {{plural_you:Corrían|Corríais}} bien; ¿quién {{plural_you:les|os}} cortó el paso para que no {{plural_you:obedezcan|obedezcáis}} a la verdad?
es.B: {{plural_you:Estaban|Estabais}} corriendo una buena carrera. ¿Quién se {{plural_you:les|os}} cruzó en el camino y {{plural_you:los|os}} apartó de obedecer la verdad?
es.R: {{plural_you:Iban|Ibais}} muy bien, como corredores en una carrera. ¿Quién {{plural_you:les|os}} cerró el paso y {{plural_you:les|os}} impidió seguir la verdad?

sw.L: Mlikuwa mkikimbia vizuri; nani aliwakatiza njiani ili msiitii kweli?
sw.B: Mlikuwa mkishindana vizuri katika mbio. Ni nani aliyewazibia njia na kuwageuza msiitii kweli?
sw.R: Mlikuwa mnaendelea vizuri sana, kama wakimbiaji katika mashindano. Nani aliwazuia njiani hata mkaacha kufuata kweli?

decisions.choice: a race: someone cut in on the runners and blocked their way
alternatives: a general word for hindering, with no picture
decisions.reason: Ἐτρέχετε pictures the Christian life as a race, as Paul does in 2:2. ἐγκόπτω was used of breaking up a road or cutting in on a runner. The imperfect tense says they were running well up to that point.

decisions.choice: to obey the truth: to keep following the gospel they believed
alternatives: to be persuaded of the truth
decisions.reason: πείθω can mean both "be persuaded" and "obey". "The truth" is the truth of the gospel (2:5, 2:14). Verse 8 plays on the same root: the new "persuasion" is not from God.

decisions.choice: you had been running a good race
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the race so the picture is clear.

source.text: ἡ πεισμονὴ οὐκ ἐκ τοῦ καλοῦντος ὑμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: The persuasion [is] not from the [one] calling you.

en.L: This persuasion [is] not from the one calling you.
en.B: That persuasion did not come from the one who calls you.
en.R: That pressure to change did not come from God, who called you.

es.L: Esta persuasión no [viene] del que {{plural_you:los|os}} llama.
es.B: Esa persuasión no vino de aquel que {{plural_you:los|os}} llama.
es.R: Esa presión para que {{plural_you:cambien|cambiéis}} no vino de Dios, que {{plural_you:los|os}} llamó.

sw.L: Ushawishi huu [hautoki] kwa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anayewaita.
sw.B: Ushawishi huo haukutoka kwa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anayewaita.
sw.R: Shinikizo hilo la kuwafanya mbadilike halikutoka kwa Mungu, aliyewaita.

decisions.choice: persuasion: the pressure the agitators were putting on them
alternatives: the Galatians' own state of being persuaded
decisions.reason: πεισμονὴ is rare and could mean the act of persuading or the state of being persuaded. It follows the verb πείθω in verse 7 as a play on words: whatever has persuaded them now did not come from God.

decisions.choice: the one calling you is God
decisions.reason: Paul has already said that God called them by grace (1:6, 1:15). The present tense speaks of God as the one who calls.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as m2 explains.

source.text: μικρὰ ζύμη ὅλον τὸ φύραμα ζυμοῖ.

records.literal_gloss: A little leaven whole the lump leavens.

en.L: A little leaven leavens all of the lump.
en.B: A little yeast spreads through all the dough.
en.R: It only takes a tiny bit of yeast to spread through a whole lump of dough.

es.L: Un poco de levadura leuda toda la masa.
es.B: Un poco de levadura se extiende por toda la masa.
es.R: Basta un poquito de levadura para que se extienda por toda la masa.

sw.L: Chachu kidogo huchachusha donge lote la unga.
sw.B: Hamira kidogo huenea katika unga wote uliokandwa.
sw.R: Hamira kidogo tu inatosha kuenea katika donge zima la unga.

decisions.choice: a proverb: a small thing spreads through the whole
decisions.reason: Paul uses the same saying in 1 Corinthians 5:6. ζύμη is leaven, a lump of old fermented dough mixed into new dough; a little works through the whole batch. Here it warns that the agitators, though few, and their teaching, though it seems a small step, will affect the whole church.

decisions.choice: yeast; spreads through
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the everyday word; Literal keeps "leaven" and the repeated root.

source.text: ἐγὼ πέποιθα εἰς ὑμᾶς ἐν κυρίῳ ὅτι οὐδὲν ἄλλο φρονήσετε· ὁ δὲ ταράσσων ὑμᾶς βαστάσει τὸ κρίμα, ὅστις ἐὰν ᾖ.

records.literal_gloss: I am confident toward you in [the] Lord that nothing other you will think; the but [one] troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever if he may be.

en.L: I am confident about you in [the] Lord that you will think nothing other; but the one troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be.
en.B: In the Lord I am confident that you will not think otherwise. But the one who is unsettling you will bear God's judgment, whoever that may be.
en.R: Because of the Lord, I trust that you will agree with me. But the person who is troubling you will face God's judgment, no matter who that is.

es.L: Yo confío respecto a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en [el] Señor que no {{plural_you:pensarán|pensaréis}} ninguna otra cosa; pero el que {{plural_you:los|os}} perturba llevará el juicio, quienquiera que sea.
es.B: En el Señor confío en que no {{plural_you:pensarán|pensaréis}} de otra manera. Pero el que {{plural_you:los|os}} está inquietando sufrirá el juicio de Dios, sea quien sea.
es.R: Gracias al Señor, confío en que {{plural_you:estarán|estaréis}} de acuerdo conmigo. Pero la persona que {{plural_you:los|os}} está perturbando tendrá que enfrentar el juicio de Dios, no importa quién sea.

sw.L: Mimi nina uhakika juu yenu katika Bwana kwamba hamtafikiri jambo lingine; lakini yeye anayewasumbua atabeba hukumu, yeyote yule awaye.
sw.B: Katika Bwana nina hakika kwamba hamtakuwa na mawazo mengine. Lakini yule anayewavuruga atabeba hukumu ya Mungu, hata awe nani.
sw.R: Kwa sababu ya Bwana, ninaamini kwamba mtakubaliana nami. Lakini mtu anayewasumbua atakabili hukumu ya Mungu, hata awe nani.

decisions.choice: Paul's confidence rests on the Lord, not on the Galatians
decisions.reason: "In the Lord" says where Paul's confidence comes from. The perfect πέποιθα speaks of a settled conviction.

decisions.choice: the one troubling you: whoever among the agitators, without exception
alternatives: a single leader of the agitators
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Paul speaks of several troublemakers (1:7, 5:12). The singular with "whoever he may be" most likely means any one of them, however important. It may point to one leader, but the letter does not name him.

decisions.choice: bear the judgment: God's judgment
decisions.reason: κρίμα with the article is the verdict that falls on such a person. As in 1:8-9, Paul leaves that judgment to God.

decisions.choice: God's judgment
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the judge (m3).

decisions.choice: you will agree with me
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "nothing other" means: no view other than the gospel Paul taught them.

source.text: ἐγὼ δέ, ἀδελφοί, εἰ περιτομὴν ἔτι κηρύσσω, τί ἔτι διώκομαι;

records.literal_gloss: I but, brothers, if circumcision still I preach, why still am I persecuted?

en.L: But I, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, if I still preach circumcision, why am I still persecuted?
en.B: As for me, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, if I am still preaching circumcision, why am I still being persecuted?
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, if I were still telling people that they must be circumcised, why would people still be attacking me?

es.L: Pero yo, hermanos, si todavía predico [la] circuncisión, ¿por qué todavía soy perseguido?
es.B: En cuanto a mí, hermanos, si todavía predico la circuncisión, ¿por qué se me sigue persiguiendo?
es.R: Hermanos, si yo siguiera diciendo a la gente que tiene que circuncidarse, ¿por qué seguirían atacándome?

sw.L: Lakini mimi, ndugu, kama bado ninahubiri tohara, kwa nini bado ninateswa?
sw.B: Na mimi, ndugu, ikiwa bado ninahubiri tohara, mbona bado ninateswa?
sw.R: Ndugu, kama ningekuwa bado ninawaambia watu kwamba lazima watahiriwe, kwa nini watu wangeendelea kunishambulia?

decisions.choice: "if I still preach circumcision": answering a claim that Paul himself required it
alternatives: Paul refers only to the time before he followed Christ
decisions.reason: The double ἔτι ("still ... still") suggests that someone was saying Paul preached circumcision when it suited him, perhaps pointing to Timothy (Acts 16:3) or to his life before his calling (1:13-14). What exactly lay behind the claim is not certain; Paul's answer is that his being persecuted proves it false.

decisions.choice: persecuted: opposed and attacked, by Jews and by those who wanted circumcision
decisions.reason: Paul's persecution came from those who saw his law-free gospel for Gentiles as a threat (4:29, 6:12; Acts 14:19).

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: As in Romans 1:13, Spanish "hermanos" already covers brothers and sisters, so there is no gender span where the English has one.

decisions.choice: ndugu, no setting
alternatives: ndugu wa kiume na wa kike
decisions.reason: As in Romans 1:13, "ndugu" already means brothers and sisters, so Swahili needs no gender span here.

source.text: ἄρα κατήργηται τὸ σκάνδαλον τοῦ σταυροῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Then has been abolished the stumbling block of the cross.

en.L: Then the stumbling block of the cross has been abolished.
en.B: In that case the cross would have stopped being a stumbling block.
en.R: If I did, the message about the cross would no longer offend anyone.

es.L: Entonces el tropiezo de la cruz ha quedado anulado.
es.B: En ese caso, la cruz habría dejado de ser piedra de tropiezo.
es.R: Si yo hiciera eso, el mensaje de la cruz ya no ofendería a nadie.

sw.L: Hapo kikwazo cha msalaba kimebatilishwa.
sw.B: Kama ndivyo, msalaba ungekuwa umeacha kuwa kikwazo.
sw.R: Kama ningefanya hivyo, ujumbe wa msalaba usingemkwaza mtu yeyote tena.

decisions.choice: the stumbling block of the cross: what offends people about a crucified Messiah
decisions.reason: σκάνδαλον is a trap or something that makes people stumble. A Messiah who died on a cross offended Jews (1 Corinthians 1:23), and a message that the cross alone saves, without circumcision, offended those who wanted to keep the law's marks (6:12).

decisions.choice: an ironic conclusion: then the offense would be gone
alternatives: a real statement that the offense has been removed
decisions.reason: ἄρα draws the conclusion of the claim in the first sentence. If Paul preached circumcision, the cross would no longer offend anyone; but it does, as his persecution shows.

decisions.choice: in that case ... would
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the irony plain by tying the sentence to the "if" of the one before.

source.text: ὄφελον καὶ ἀποκόψονται οἱ ἀναστατοῦντες ὑμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: Would that even will cut themselves off those unsettling you.

en.L: I wish that those unsettling you would even cut themselves off!
en.B: As for those who are stirring you up, I wish they would go the whole way and castrate themselves!
en.R: I wish the people who are upsetting you would go further than circumcision and castrate themselves!

es.L: ¡Ojalá incluso se cortaran ellos mismos los que {{plural_you:los|os}} alborotan!
es.B: En cuanto a los que {{plural_you:los|os}} están alborotando, ¡ojalá llegaran hasta el final y se castraran!
es.R: ¡Ojalá que la gente que {{plural_you:los|os}} está trastornando fuera más allá de la circuncisión y se castrara!

sw.L: Ningependa hata wajikate wenyewe, hao wanaowavuruga!
sw.B: Kuhusu hao wanaowachochea, natamani waende mbali kabisa wajihasi wenyewe!
sw.R: Natamani watu hao wanaowasumbua waende zaidi ya tohara, wajihasi kabisa!

decisions.choice: castrate themselves: a coarse play on circumcision
alternatives: cut themselves off from the church
decisions.reason: ἀποκόπτω means "cut off". Used of the body, and with "even" after a passage about circumcision, it most naturally means to cut off the male organ altogether. Paul says that if the agitators are so keen on cutting, they might go all the way. Some have read it as a wish that they would cut themselves off from the church, but that does not explain "even". The pagan priests of the goddess Cybele, known in Galatia, castrated themselves; Paul's words would put circumcision demanded as a condition on the same level.

decisions.choice: a wish that is not expected to come true
decisions.reason: ὄφελον with a future verb expresses a wish, here a bitter and sarcastic one.

decisions.choice: those unsettling you: stirring them up and turning them upside down
decisions.reason: ἀναστατόω is used of stirring up a revolt (Acts 17:6, 21:38); it is stronger than "troubling" in verse 10.

decisions.choice: castrate themselves
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what the verb means here (m1); Literal keeps "cut themselves off", with its double sense.

source.text: Ὑμεῖς γὰρ ἐπ’ ἐλευθερίᾳ ἐκλήθητε, ἀδελφοί· μόνον μὴ τὴν ἐλευθερίαν εἰς ἀφορμὴν τῇ σαρκί, ἀλλὰ διὰ τῆς ἀγάπης δουλεύετε ἀλλήλοις·

records.literal_gloss: You for to freedom were called, brothers; only not the freedom into an opening for the flesh, but through the love serve as slaves one another;

en.L: For you were called to freedom, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}; only [do] not [turn] the freedom into an opening for the flesh, but through love serve one another as slaves.
en.B: You were called to be free, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}. Only do not let your freedom become an opening for the flesh. Instead, through love, be slaves to one another.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, God called you to be free. But do not treat your freedom as a chance to give your sinful self what it wants. Instead, love one another and serve one another like slaves.

es.L: Porque {{plural_you:ustedes fueron|vosotros fuisteis}} llamados a [la] libertad, hermanos; solo que no [{{plural_you:conviertan|convirtáis}}] la libertad en ocasión para la carne, sino {{plural_you:sírvanse|servíos}} como esclavos unos a otros por medio del amor.
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes fueron|Vosotros fuisteis}} llamados a ser libres, hermanos. Solo que no {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} libertad se convierta en una puerta abierta para la carne. Al contrario, por medio del amor, {{plural_you:háganse|haceos}} esclavos unos de otros.
es.R: Hermanos, Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} llamó a ser libres. Pero no {{plural_you:usen|uséis}} {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} libertad como excusa para darle a {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} yo pecador lo que quiere. Al contrario, {{plural_you:ámense|amaos}} unos a otros y {{plural_you:sírvanse|servíos}} unos a otros como esclavos.

sw.L: Kwa maana ninyi mliitwa kwa ajili ya uhuru, ndugu; ila tu [msiufanye] uhuru kuwa mwanya kwa mwili, bali kupitia upendo kuweni watumwa ninyi kwa ninyi.
sw.B: Ninyi mliitwa ili muwe huru, ndugu. Ila tu msiruhusu uhuru wenu uwe mwanya kwa asili ya dhambi. Badala yake, kwa upendo, kuweni watumwa ninyi kwa ninyi.
sw.R: Ndugu, Mungu aliwaita muwe huru. Lakini msiutumie uhuru wenu kama nafasi ya kuipa asili yenu ya dhambi kile inachotaka. Badala yake, pendaneni, na mtumikiane kama watumwa.

decisions.choice: the sinful human self opposed to the Spirit
decisions.reason: In 5:13-24 σαρκί is not the body as such but human life apart from God and turned against him: it has desires (5:16-17), works (5:19) and can be crucified (5:24), and it stands against the Spirit. The word keeps its link with the circumcised "flesh" the agitators boast in (6:12-13).

decisions.choice: an opening: a base from which to launch an attack
decisions.reason: ἀφορμὴν was used of a starting point or base for military operations. Freedom must not give the flesh a foothold.

decisions.choice: serve as slaves: freedom used to become one another's slaves in love
decisions.reason: δουλεύω is the verb of being a slave, the same root as the "slavery" of 5:1 and 4:3, 4:8-9. The paradox is deliberate: those freed from the law's yoke give themselves to one another out of love.

decisions.choice: your sinful self
decisions.reason: Readable says what "flesh" means here (m1); Literal and Balanced keep "flesh".

decisions.choice: God called you
decisions.reason: Readable names the one who called, as in 1:6 and 5:8.

decisions.choice: carne (L, B); yo pecador (R)
decisions.reason: Recorded once for the flesh and Spirit passage (5:13-6:8). Here "flesh" is the sinful human self opposed to the Spirit (m1). In Spanish "la carne" in phrases like "los deseos de la carne" is the long-familiar way of naming that self, so Literal and Balanced keep "carne", as the English Balanced keeps "flesh" and as Romans 13:14 does. Readable says "yo pecador" (sinful self), the wording Romans 13:14 uses, with the plural_you possessive "su|vuestro". "Espíritu" is capitalised throughout: it is God's Spirit.

decisions.choice: esclavos (sírvanse como esclavos / háganse esclavos)
decisions.reason: δουλεύετε is the verb of being a slave, from the root of "esclavitud" in 5:1 (m3). "Servir" alone would lose Paul's paradox, so every level says "esclavos", as the style guide keeps the slave word where slavery is set against freedom in the same sentence.

decisions.choice: mwili (L); asili ya dhambi (B, R)
decisions.reason: Recorded once for the flesh and Spirit passage (5:13-6:8). "Mwili" is the body, and "tamaa za mwili" would sound like bodily appetites only. Here the word means the sinful human self opposed to the Spirit (m1), so Balanced and Readable say "asili ya dhambi" (sinful nature), as in Romans 13:14; Literal keeps "mwili". Roho (the Spirit) takes personal agreement ("Roho anatamani", "Roho anawaongoza").

decisions.choice: kuweni watumwa ninyi kwa ninyi
decisions.reason: "Tumikianeni" (serve one another) would lose the slave word. "Watumwa" keeps the link with "utumwa" in 5:1 and Paul's paradox (m3); Readable adds "kama watumwa" to the plainer verb.

decisions.choice: serve as slaves / be slaves / serve like slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slavery is set against freedom in the same sentence: those called to freedom become one another's slaves in love, a deliberate paradox (m3).

source.text: ὁ γὰρ πᾶς νόμος ἐν ἑνὶ λόγῳ πεπλήρωται, ἐν τῷ· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν.

records.literal_gloss: The for whole law in one word has been fulfilled, in the: You shall love the neighbor of you as yourself.

en.L: For the whole law has been fulfilled in one word, in this: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself."
en.B: The whole law comes to its fullness in one sentence: "You must love your neighbor as you love yourself."
en.R: Everything the law asks is done when you keep this one command: "Love your neighbor as much as you love yourself."

es.L: Porque toda la ley se ha cumplido en una sola palabra, en esta: «Amarás a tu prójimo como a ti mismo».
es.B: Toda la ley alcanza su plenitud en una sola frase: «Debes amar a tu prójimo como te amas a ti mismo».
es.R: Todo lo que pide la ley se cumple cuando alguien obedece este único mandamiento: «Ama a tu prójimo tanto como te amas a ti mismo».

sw.L: Kwa maana sheria yote imetimizwa katika neno moja, katika hili: "Utampenda jirani yako kama wewe mwenyewe."
sw.B: Sheria yote inafikia utimilifu wake katika neno hili moja: "Mpende jirani yako kama unavyojipenda mwenyewe."
sw.R: Yote ambayo sheria inataka yanatimizwa mtu anaposhika amri hii moja: "Mpende jirani yako kama vile unavyojipenda mwenyewe."

decisions.choice: a quotation of Leviticus 19:18
decisions.reason: Paul quotes the command to love one's neighbor from Leviticus 19:18, in the words of the Greek translation of the Old Testament. Jesus named it as the second great command (Mark 12:31), and Paul uses it the same way in Romans 13:8-10.

decisions.choice: fulfilled: the law's whole aim is reached and done in love
alternatives: summed up only, as a summary
decisions.reason: πεπλήρωται is perfect: the law has been fulfilled. Paul does not only mean that one command sums up the rest; when people love, what the law was aiming at actually happens. Those who are not under the law (5:18) still fulfill it by love.

decisions.choice: one word: one saying, a single command
decisions.reason: λόγῳ here is one sentence of Scripture, not one word.

source.text: εἰ δὲ ἀλλήλους δάκνετε καὶ κατεσθίετε, βλέπετε μὴ ὑπ’ ἀλλήλων ἀναλωθῆτε.

records.literal_gloss: If but one another you bite and devour, watch lest by one another you be consumed.

en.L: But if you bite and devour one another, watch lest you be used up by one another.
en.B: But if you keep biting one another and tearing each other apart, be careful, or you will end up destroying one another.
en.R: But if you keep attacking each other like wild animals, watch out! You will end up wiping each other out.

es.L: Pero si {{plural_you:se muerden|os mordéis}} y {{plural_you:se devoran|os devoráis}} unos a otros, {{plural_you:miren|mirad}} que no {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} consumidos unos por otros.
es.B: Pero si {{plural_you:se siguen|os seguís}} mordiendo y despedazando unos a otros, {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} cuidado, o {{plural_you:se destruirán|os destruiréis}} unos a otros.
es.R: Pero si {{plural_you:se siguen|os seguís}} atacando unos a otros como fieras, ¡cuidado! Al final {{plural_you:se van|os vais}} a destruir unos a otros.

sw.L: Lakini kama mnaumana na kutafunana ninyi kwa ninyi, jihadharini msije mkamalizwa ninyi kwa ninyi.
sw.B: Lakini mkiendelea kuumana na kuraruana, jihadharini, la sivyo mtaishia kuangamizana.
sw.R: Lakini mkiendelea kushambuliana kama wanyama wa porini, jihadharini! Mtaishia kumalizana kabisa.

decisions.choice: biting, devouring, consuming: wild animals fighting until they destroy each other
decisions.reason: The three verbs picture animals tearing at one another; ἀναλίσκω means to use up or destroy entirely. The present tenses suggest the quarrels had already begun.

decisions.choice: attacking each other like wild animals
decisions.reason: Readable names the picture so it is not taken literally.

source.text: Λέγω δέ, πνεύματι περιπατεῖτε καὶ ἐπιθυμίαν σαρκὸς οὐ μὴ τελέσητε.

records.literal_gloss: I say but, by [the] Spirit walk and [the] desire of flesh not not you will carry out.

en.L: But I say, walk by [the] Spirit, and you will certainly not carry out [the] desire of [the] flesh.
en.B: This is what I mean: walk by the Spirit, and you will never carry out what the flesh desires.
en.R: So this is what I am saying: let the Spirit guide your steps each day. Then you will never do what your sinful self wants.

es.L: Pero digo: {{plural_you:anden|andad}} por [el] Espíritu, y de ningún modo {{plural_you:llevarán|llevaréis}} a cabo [el] deseo de [la] carne.
es.B: Esto es lo que quiero decir: {{plural_you:anden|andad}} por el Espíritu, y nunca {{plural_you:harán|haréis}} lo que la carne desea.
es.R: Así que esto es lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: {{plural_you:dejen|dejad}} que el Espíritu guíe {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} pasos cada día. Así nunca {{plural_you:harán|haréis}} lo que {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} yo pecador quiere.

sw.L: Ila nasema hivi: tembeeni kwa Roho, na hakika hamtaitekeleza tamaa ya mwili.
sw.B: Hiki ndicho ninachomaanisha: ishini mkiongozwa na Roho, nanyi hamtatenda kamwe yale ambayo asili ya dhambi inatamani.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo ninachosema ni hiki: mwacheni Roho aongoze hatua zenu kila siku. Hapo hamtafanya kamwe kile ambacho asili yenu ya dhambi inataka.

decisions.choice: the sinful human self opposed to the Spirit
decisions.reason: In 5:13-24 σαρκὸς is not the body as such but human life apart from God and turned against him: it has desires (5:16-17), works (5:19) and can be crucified (5:24), and it stands against the Spirit. The word keeps its link with the circumcised "flesh" the agitators boast in (6:12-13).

decisions.choice: a promise: you will certainly not carry out what the flesh desires
alternatives: a second command: and do not carry out the flesh's desire
decisions.reason: οὐ μὴ with the aorist subjunctive is the strongest way Greek says "will not". It promises the result of walking by the Spirit; it is not a further command.

decisions.choice: walk by the Spirit: live day by day as the Spirit directs and empowers
decisions.reason: περιπατέω ("walk") is the usual biblical word for how a person lives. The dative πνεύματι says the Spirit is the power and guide of that life.

decisions.choice: let the Spirit guide your steps each day
decisions.reason: Readable explains the walking picture.

decisions.choice: your sinful self
decisions.reason: Readable says what "flesh" means here (m1).

decisions.choice: ishini mkiongozwa na Roho
decisions.reason: περιπατεῖτε is the usual biblical picture for how one lives (m3). Swahili "kutembea" suggests a stroll, so Balanced says "ishini mkiongozwa na Roho" (live led by the Spirit) where the English Balanced keeps "walk"; Literal keeps "tembeeni".

source.text: ἡ γὰρ σὰρξ ἐπιθυμεῖ κατὰ τοῦ πνεύματος, τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα κατὰ τῆς σαρκός, ταῦτα γὰρ ἀλλήλοις ἀντίκειται, ἵνα μὴ ἃ ἐὰν θέλητε ταῦτα ποιῆτε.

records.literal_gloss: The for flesh desires against the Spirit, the and Spirit against the flesh, these for to one another are opposed, so that not whatever things you may want these you may do.

en.L: For the flesh desires against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh, for these are opposed to one another, so that you do not do whatever things you want.
en.B: For the flesh sets its desires against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh. They are at war with each other, so that you are not free to do whatever you please.
en.R: What your sinful self wants is against what the Spirit wants, and what the Spirit wants is against your sinful self. The two are at war with each other. So you cannot just do whatever you feel like doing.

es.L: Porque la carne desea contra el Espíritu, y el Espíritu contra la carne, pues estos se oponen entre sí, para que no {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} las cosas que {{plural_you:quieran|queráis}}.
es.B: Porque la carne dirige sus deseos contra el Espíritu, y el Espíritu contra la carne. Están en guerra entre sí, de modo que no {{plural_you:son|sois}} libres para hacer lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} plazca.
es.R: Lo que {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} yo pecador quiere va en contra de lo que quiere el Espíritu, y lo que quiere el Espíritu va en contra de {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} yo pecador. Los dos están en guerra. Por eso no {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} hacer simplemente lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} dé la gana.

sw.L: Kwa maana mwili hutamani kinyume cha Roho, na Roho kinyume cha mwili, kwa maana hivi viwili vinapingana, ili msiyafanye yale mnayotaka.
sw.B: Kwa maana asili ya dhambi inatamani mambo yaliyo kinyume na Roho, na Roho anatamani yaliyo kinyume na asili ya dhambi. Viwili hivi viko vitani, hivyo hamko huru kufanya lolote mnalotaka.
sw.R: Kile ambacho asili yenu ya dhambi inataka ni kinyume na kile Roho anachotaka, na kile Roho anachotaka ni kinyume na asili yenu ya dhambi. Hivi viwili vinapigana. Kwa hiyo hamwezi kufanya tu chochote mnachojisikia kufanya.

decisions.choice: the sinful human self opposed to the Spirit
decisions.reason: In 5:13-24 σὰρξ is not the body as such but human life apart from God and turned against him: it has desires (5:16-17), works (5:19) and can be crucified (5:24), and it stands against the Spirit. The word keeps its link with the circumcised "flesh" the agitators boast in (6:12-13).

decisions.choice: so that you do not simply do whatever you want: the conflict leaves no room for doing as you please
alternatives: the flesh keeps you from doing the good you want
the Spirit keeps you from doing what the flesh wants
decisions.reason: ἵνα can express purpose or result, and Paul does not say which wishes are blocked. The flesh may hinder the good a person wants (compare Romans 7:15-20), or the Spirit may hold back the flesh's desires, as verse 16 promises. Read with verse 13, the point seems to be that freedom is not doing as one likes: a person is in a battle and must follow the Spirit (verse 18).

decisions.choice: at war with each other
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the strength of the word for opposing.

decisions.choice: your sinful self
decisions.reason: Readable says what "flesh" means here (m1).

source.text: εἰ δὲ πνεύματι ἄγεσθε, οὐκ ἐστὲ ὑπὸ νόμον.

records.literal_gloss: If but by [the] Spirit you are led, not you are under law.

en.L: But if you are led by [the] Spirit, you are not under [the] law.
en.B: But if the Spirit is leading you, you are not under the law.
en.R: But if the Spirit is leading you, then the law is not your master.

es.L: Pero si {{plural_you:son|sois}} guiados por [el] Espíritu, no {{plural_you:están|estáis}} bajo [la] ley.
es.B: Pero si el Espíritu {{plural_you:los|os}} guía, no {{plural_you:están|estáis}} bajo la ley.
es.R: Pero si el Espíritu {{plural_you:los|os}} está guiando, entonces la ley no es {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} amo.

sw.L: Lakini ikiwa mnaongozwa na Roho, hamko chini ya sheria.
sw.B: Lakini ikiwa Roho anawaongoza, hamko chini ya sheria.
sw.R: Lakini ikiwa Roho anawaongoza, basi sheria haiwatawali tena.

decisions.choice: under law: living under the law's rule as guardian and master
decisions.reason: Paul has used "under law" for the time before Christ, when the law held people as a guardian holds a child (3:23-25, 4:4-5). Those led by the Spirit are no longer under that regime, yet they are not left without guidance: the Spirit leads them.

decisions.choice: "if" describes what is true of believers: they are led by the Spirit
decisions.reason: εἰ with the present indicative assumes the condition; compare Romans 8:14, where all who are led by God's Spirit are God's children.

decisions.choice: the law is not your master
alternatives: you are not under the law
decisions.reason: Readable explains "under" as being ruled (m1).

source.text: φανερὰ δέ ἐστιν τὰ ἔργα τῆς σαρκός, ἅτινά ἐστιν πορνεία, ἀκαθαρσία, ἀσέλγεια, εἰδωλολατρία, φαρμακεία, ἔχθραι, ἔρις, ζῆλος, θυμοί, ἐριθεῖαι, διχοστασίαι, αἱρέσεις, φθόνοι, μέθαι, κῶμοι, καὶ τὰ ὅμοια τούτοις, ἃ προλέγω ὑμῖν καθὼς προεῖπον ὅτι οἱ τὰ τοιαῦτα πράσσοντες βασιλείαν θεοῦ οὐ κληρονομήσουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Evident and are the works of the flesh, which are sexual immorality, impurity, indecency, \v 20 idolatry, sorcery, hostilities, strife, jealousy, angers, rivalries, dissensions, factions, \v 21 envyings, drunkennesses, revelries, and the things like these, which I tell beforehand to you just as I said before, that the [ones] the such things practicing [the] kingdom of God not will inherit.

en.L: Now the works of the flesh are evident, which are sexual immorality, impurity, indecency, \v 20 idolatry, sorcery, hostilities, strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, selfish rivalries, dissensions, factions, \v 21 envyings, drunken bouts, revelries, and the things like these, about which I tell you beforehand, just as I said before, that those who practice such things will not inherit [the] kingdom of God.
en.B: The works of the flesh are plain to see: sexual immorality, impurity, indecency, \v 20 idolatry, sorcery, hostility, quarreling, jealousy, fits of rage, selfish rivalry, divisions, factions, \v 21 envy, drunken bouts, wild partying, and other things like these. I am telling you now, as I told you before: people who live this way will not inherit the kingdom of God.
en.R: It is easy to see what the sinful self does: sexual sin, impure living, shameless behavior, \v 20 worshiping idols, using magic, hating people, fighting, being jealous, losing your temper, putting yourself first, splitting into sides and groups, \v 21 envying others, getting drunk, wild parties, and other things like these. I warned you before, and I am warning you again: people who keep doing such things will not receive God's kingdom as their inheritance.

es.L: Y las obras de la carne son manifiestas, las cuales son: inmoralidad sexual, impureza, desenfreno, \v 20 idolatría, hechicería, enemistades, discordia, celos, estallidos de ira, ambiciones egoístas, divisiones, partidismos, \v 21 envidias, borracheras, juergas, y cosas parecidas a estas, acerca de las cuales {{plural_you:les|os}} digo de antemano, tal como {{plural_you:les|os}} dije antes, que los que se dedican a tales cosas no heredarán [el] reino de Dios.
es.B: Las obras de la carne están a la vista: inmoralidad sexual, impureza, indecencia, \v 20 idolatría, hechicería, hostilidad, peleas, celos, ataques de furia, rivalidad egoísta, divisiones, bandos, \v 21 envidia, borracheras, parrandas desenfrenadas y otras cosas como estas. Ahora {{plural_you:les|os}} lo advierto, como ya {{plural_you:les|os}} lo había dicho: los que viven así no heredarán el reino de Dios.
es.R: Es fácil ver lo que produce el yo pecador: pecados sexuales, una vida impura, conducta sin vergüenza, \v 20 adorar ídolos, practicar la magia, odiar a la gente, pelear, tener celos, perder los estribos, pensar solo en uno mismo, dividirse en partidos y grupos, \v 21 envidiar a otros, emborracharse, fiestas desenfrenadas y otras cosas como estas. Ya {{plural_you:les|os}} lo advertí antes, y {{plural_you:les|os}} lo vuelvo a advertir: la gente que sigue haciendo tales cosas no recibirá el reino de Dios como herencia.

sw.L: Basi matendo ya mwili yako wazi, nayo ni: zinaa, unajisi, ukosefu wa haya, \v 20 kuabudu sanamu, uchawi, chuki, mabishano, wivu, milipuko ya hasira, ubinafsi, migawanyiko, makundi, \v 21 kijicho, ulevi, sherehe za anasa, na mambo yanayofanana na hayo; kuhusu hayo nawaonya mapema, kama nilivyosema hapo awali, kwamba wanaoyatenda mambo ya namna hiyo hawataurithi ufalme wa Mungu.
sw.B: Matendo ya asili ya dhambi yanaonekana wazi: zinaa, unajisi, tabia isiyo na haya, \v 20 kuabudu sanamu, uchawi, uhasama, magomvi, wivu, hasira kali za ghafla, kujitafutia makuu, mgawanyiko, makundi, \v 21 kijicho, ulevi, sherehe za anasa, na mambo mengine kama hayo. Nawaambia sasa, kama nilivyowaambia kabla: watu wanaoishi hivyo hawataurithi ufalme wa Mungu.
sw.R: Ni rahisi kuona yale ambayo asili ya dhambi hutenda: dhambi za ngono, maisha machafu, tabia za aibu, \v 20 kuabudu sanamu, kufanya uchawi, kuwachukia watu, kugombana, kuona wivu, kukasirika upesi, kujiweka mbele, kugawanyika katika pande na vikundi, \v 21 kuwaonea wengine kijicho, kulewa, sherehe za anasa, na mambo mengine kama hayo. Niliwaonya zamani, na sasa ninawaonya tena: watu wanaoendelea kufanya mambo kama hayo hawatapokea ufalme wa Mungu kama urithi wao.

decisions.choice: the sinful human self opposed to the Spirit
decisions.reason: In 5:13-24 σαρκός is not the body as such but human life apart from God and turned against him: it has desires (5:16-17), works (5:19) and can be crucified (5:24), and it stands against the Spirit. The word keeps its link with the circumcised "flesh" the agitators boast in (6:12-13).

decisions.choice: sorcery: magic and spells, which often used drugs and potions
alternatives: the use of drugs or poisons in general
decisions.reason: φαρμακεία comes from the word for a drug, but in lists like this it means magic arts, in which potions were used to curse, charm or harm (compare Revelation 9:21, 18:23). It stands next to idolatry as a sin against God.

decisions.choice: selfish rivalry; factions: people splitting into parties
alternatives: "heresies" in the later sense of false doctrine
decisions.reason: ἐριθεῖαι is the self-seeking of someone out for himself or his party. αἱρέσεις here means groups that take sides against each other, as in 1 Corinthians 11:19, not yet a technical word for false teaching.

decisions.choice: those who practice such things: a settled way of life
alternatives: anyone who has ever done one of them
decisions.reason: The present participle πράσσοντες describes people who go on doing these things. Paul warns that such a life shows a person does not belong to God's kingdom; the same warning comes in 1 Corinthians 6:9-11, which speaks of people who were washed from such a life.

decisions.choice: Paul had warned them of this before, while he was with them
decisions.reason: προεῖπον ("I said before") points back to his teaching when he founded the churches (compare 1:9, 4:13).

decisions.choice: indecency / shameless behavior
decisions.reason: ἀσέλγεια is open, shameless indecency; Balanced and Readable use words a reader will understand without a dictionary.

decisions.choice: your sinful self
decisions.reason: Readable says what "flesh" means here (m1).

decisions.choice: receive God's kingdom as their inheritance
decisions.reason: Readable explains "inherit": to receive what belongs to God's children (4:7).

decisions.choice: zinaa; ukosefu wa haya / tabia isiyo na haya; kijicho; sherehe za anasa
decisions.reason: The vice list is drafted from the Greek in everyday standard words. "Ufisadi" now usually means corruption (graft), so ἀσέλγεια is "ukosefu wa haya" (shamelessness); "kijicho" is the common word for envy; κῶμοι is "sherehe za anasa", as in Romans 13:13. "Hasira" is used for human anger, keeping "ghadhabu" for God's wrath. A native reviewer should check each term.

source.text: Ὁ δὲ καρπὸς τοῦ πνεύματός ἐστιν ἀγάπη, χαρά, εἰρήνη, μακροθυμία, χρηστότης, ἀγαθωσύνη, πίστις, πραΰτης, ἐγκράτεια· κατὰ τῶν τοιούτων οὐκ ἔστιν νόμος.

records.literal_gloss: The but fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, long-suffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, \v 23 gentleness, self-control; against the such things not there is law.

en.L: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, \v 23 gentleness, self-control; against such things there is no law.
en.B: But the fruit the Spirit produces is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, \v 23 gentleness and self-control. No law stands against things like these.
en.R: But the Spirit grows a different crop in us: love, joy and peace; patience with others, kindness and goodness; faithfulness, \v 23 gentleness and self-control. There is no law against things like these.

es.L: Pero el fruto del Espíritu es amor, gozo, paz, paciencia, amabilidad, bondad, fidelidad, \v 23 mansedumbre, dominio de sí mismo; contra tales cosas no hay ley.
es.B: Pero el fruto que produce el Espíritu es amor, gozo, paz, paciencia, amabilidad, bondad, fidelidad, \v 23 mansedumbre y dominio de sí mismo. Ninguna ley se opone a cosas como estas.
es.R: Pero el Espíritu hace crecer en nosotros una cosecha muy distinta: amor, alegría y paz; paciencia con los demás, amabilidad y bondad; fidelidad, \v 23 trato apacible y dominio de sí mismo. No hay ninguna ley contra cosas así.

sw.L: Lakini tunda la Roho ni upendo, furaha, amani, subira, fadhili, wema, uaminifu, \v 23 upole, kujitawala; dhidi ya mambo kama hayo hakuna sheria.
sw.B: Lakini tunda ambalo Roho huzaa ni upendo, furaha, amani, subira, fadhili, wema, uaminifu, \v 23 upole na kujitawala. Hakuna sheria inayopinga mambo kama haya.
sw.R: Lakini Roho huotesha ndani yetu mavuno tofauti kabisa: upendo, furaha na amani; subira kwa wengine, fadhili na wema; uaminifu, \v 23 upole na kujitawala. Hakuna sheria inayokataza mambo kama haya.

decisions.choice: the fruit of the Spirit: one harvest, which the Spirit produces
alternatives: separate fruits, any one of which a person may have
decisions.reason: καρπὸς is singular, set against the plural "works" of the flesh (verse 19). The qualities belong together as one crop that grows from the Spirit's life in a person, not as achievements of human effort.

decisions.choice: faithfulness: being reliable and true to others
decisions.reason: In this list of qualities shown toward others, πίστις means faithfulness, the sense it has in Romans 3:3 and Titus 2:10. Elsewhere in Galatians the same word means trust in Christ, but here it stands between goodness and gentleness as part of a person's character.

decisions.choice: peace: wholeness and harmony, with God and with one another
decisions.reason: εἰρήνη here stands against the strife and divisions of verse 20; it is peace among people as well as peace with God.

decisions.choice: patience: bearing with people for a long time without anger
decisions.reason: μακροθυμία is "long temper", slowness to anger, usually toward people who wrong or provoke us.

decisions.choice: against such things: the qualities just listed
decisions.reason: τοιούτων could be neuter ("such things") or masculine ("such people"). The meaning is close either way: no law forbids or condemns a life like this.

decisions.choice: faithfulness
decisions.reason: The key term is rendered "faithfulness" here because of its sense in this list (m2).

decisions.choice: the Spirit grows a different crop in us
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture of the fruit and the contrast with verse 19.

decisions.choice: fidelidad
decisions.reason: In this list πίστις is faithfulness (m2), so Spanish says "fidelidad" rather than the settled "fe" used where it means trust in Christ.

decisions.choice: tunda la Roho; uaminifu
decisions.reason: "Tunda" stays singular, as καρπὸς is (m1), against the plural "matendo" of verse 19. πίστις here is faithfulness (m2), so Swahili says "uaminifu" rather than the settled "imani".

source.text: οἱ δὲ τοῦ Χριστοῦ τὴν σάρκα ἐσταύρωσαν σὺν τοῖς παθήμασιν καὶ ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις.

records.literal_gloss: Those and of the Christ the flesh crucified with the passions and the desires.

en.L: And those of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} have crucified the flesh with the passions and the desires.
en.B: Those who belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} have nailed the flesh to the cross, together with its passions and desires.
en.R: People who belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} have put their sinful self to death on the cross, with all its strong feelings and desires.

es.L: Y los {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} han crucificado la carne con las pasiones y los deseos.
es.B: Los que pertenecen {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}} han clavado la carne en la cruz, junto con sus pasiones y sus deseos.
es.R: Las personas que pertenecen {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}} han hecho morir en la cruz a su yo pecador, con todos sus sentimientos fuertes y sus deseos.

sw.L: Na wale wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} wameusulubisha mwili pamoja na mihemko na tamaa.
sw.B: Wale ambao ni wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} wameigongomea msalabani asili ya dhambi, pamoja na mihemko yake na tamaa zake.
sw.R: Watu walio wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} wameiua asili yao ya dhambi msalabani, pamoja na hisia zake zote kali na tamaa zake.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "those of Christ"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "Jesus" after "Christ". The SBLGNT text follows early manuscripts that have "Christ" alone. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the sinful human self opposed to the Spirit
decisions.reason: In 5:13-24 σάρκα is not the body as such but human life apart from God and turned against him: it has desires (5:16-17), works (5:19) and can be crucified (5:24), and it stands against the Spirit. The word keeps its link with the circumcised "flesh" the agitators boast in (6:12-13).

decisions.choice: they crucified the flesh: a decisive act when they came to belong to Christ
alternatives: a continuing effort to kill the flesh
decisions.reason: ἐσταύρωσαν is an aorist active verb: it looks back to something done. In 2:19-20 Paul has been crucified with Christ, and in 6:14 the world has been crucified to him. Those who belong to Christ have taken his side against the flesh once for all; walking by the Spirit (verse 25) lives that out.

decisions.choice: nailed the flesh to the cross
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of crucifixion vivid; Literal keeps "crucified".

decisions.choice: put their sinful self to death on the cross
decisions.reason: Readable says what "flesh" means here (m2) and what crucifying it does.

source.text: εἰ ζῶμεν πνεύματι, πνεύματι καὶ στοιχῶμεν.

records.literal_gloss: If we live by [the] Spirit, by [the] Spirit also let us keep in line.

en.L: If we live by [the] Spirit, let us also keep in line with [the] Spirit.
en.B: Since our life comes from the Spirit, let us also follow the Spirit's lead in each step we take.
en.R: The Spirit has given us life. So let us also follow the Spirit, one step at a time.

es.L: Si vivimos por [el] Espíritu, andemos también en línea con [el] Espíritu.
es.B: Ya que nuestra vida viene del Espíritu, sigamos también la guía del Espíritu en cada paso que demos.
es.R: El Espíritu nos ha dado vida. Así que sigamos también al Espíritu, paso a paso.

sw.L: Kama tunaishi kwa Roho, na tujipange pia sawasawa na Roho.
sw.B: Kwa kuwa uzima wetu unatoka kwa Roho, na tufuate uongozi wa Roho katika kila hatua tunayopiga.
sw.R: Roho ametupa uzima. Kwa hiyo na tumfuate Roho, hatua kwa hatua.

decisions.choice: "if we live by the Spirit": since we do
decisions.reason: εἰ with the indicative assumes the fact: believers have life from the Spirit (3:3, 3:5, 4:6).

decisions.choice: keep in line with the Spirit: follow the Spirit's lead step by step
decisions.reason: στοιχέω means to stand or move in a line, as soldiers in rank or plants in a row, and so to follow a rule or pattern. Paul uses the same verb in 6:16. It is a different word from "walk" in verse 16.

decisions.choice: follow the Spirit's lead
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express the picture of keeping in line in plain words.

source.text: μὴ γινώμεθα κενόδοξοι, ἀλλήλους προκαλούμενοι, ἀλλήλοις φθονοῦντες.

records.literal_gloss: Not let us become vainglorious, one another challenging, one another envying.

en.L: Let us not become vainglorious, challenging one another, envying one another.
en.B: We must not become people hungry for empty praise, who challenge one another and envy one another.
en.R: We should not show off to get people's praise. We should not try to beat each other or be jealous of each other.

es.L: No lleguemos a ser vanagloriosos, desafiándonos unos a otros, envidiándonos unos a otros.
es.B: No nos convirtamos en gente hambrienta de alabanza vacía, que se desafía y se envidia mutuamente.
es.R: No presumamos para que la gente nos alabe. No tratemos de ganarles a los demás ni tengamos envidia unos de otros.

sw.L: Tusiwe wenye kutafuta sifa tupu, tukichokozana, tukioneana wivu.
sw.B: Tusiwe watu wenye kiu ya sifa zisizo na maana, wanaochokozana na kuoneana wivu.
sw.R: Tusijionyeshe ili watu watusifu. Tusijaribu kushindana na wenzetu wala kuoneana wivu.

decisions.choice: vainglorious: hungry for empty praise
decisions.reason: κενόδοξοι is made from "empty" and "glory": someone eager for honor that has no worth.

decisions.choice: two sides of the same sin: those who feel above others challenge them; those who feel below envy them
decisions.reason: προκαλέομαι is to call someone out, to challenge him to a contest. φθονέω is to envy. Both come from wanting empty glory, and both destroy the love Paul has called for (verses 13-15).

decisions.choice: vainglorious
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the two parts of the Greek word.

decisions.choice: sifa tupu
decisions.reason: κενόδοξοι joins "empty" and "glory" (m1). The settled "utukufu" is kept for God's glory, so Swahili names the empty honour people chase as "sifa" (praise).
